newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma to meet top IMF official-dep min.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma to meet top IMF official-dep min.

text.p: Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma will meet a top International Monetary Fund official this week to review progress in meeting conditions for a multi-billion dollar credit, an Economy Ministry official said on Wednesday.
"It is a one-day working visit," Ihor Shumylo, a deputy Economy Minister, told a news conference about the visit of IMF deputy managing director Stanley Fischer on Thursday.
Ukraine must meet 41 conditions before it qualifies to receive the three-year, $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility, in part delayed because of the 1997 budget -- now almost six months late.
"The visit foresees a meeting with the highest leaders of our country and talks about the mutual work of Ukraine and the IMF, including preparation for the Extended Fund Facility," Shumylo said.
He said passage of the budget is a major but not sole condition for Ukraine to receive the credit, succeeding an $867 million stand-by agreement which expired in February.

Shumylo added Ukraine had fulfilled 27 of the 41 conditions and the IMF had agreed to delay some of them by several months, such as cancellation of export taxes on livestock and leather, and pension reform.
Ukraine could receive the credit as early as next month, he added.
The budget is being passed in concert with nine tax laws designed to reform Ukraine's onerous and punitive tax system.
